pages.title: Playwright rewind · TypeScript
pages.description: Prepare browser state, checkpoint it, rewind, reconnect, and verify the restored value with TypeScript.
pages.intro: This self-contained example makes a post-checkpoint edit, rewinds it, reconnects because the old Playwright handles are stale, and verifies the captured value.

pages.title: Playwright rewind · Python
pages.description: Prepare browser state, checkpoint it, rewind, reconnect, and verify the restored value with Python.
pages.intro: This is the synchronous Python equivalent of the TypeScript rewind flow, including the terminal operation wait before the later close mutation.

pages.title: Playwright fork · TypeScript
pages.description: Fork ordered Playwright branches from checkpointed state and verify every child inherited it.
pages.intro: The source prepares state before the checkpoint, changes the source afterward, forks one or more peer sessions, and verifies that every child received the checkpointed value.
pages.success: The default three-session organization limit supports `BRAWSR_FORK_N=1` or `2`. Fork-10 requires capacity for the source plus ten children.

pages.title: Speculative branching
pages.description: Evaluate two inherited browser branches concurrently and keep result selection in application policy.
pages.intro: This pattern uses the default three-session limit: one source and two children. It verifies inherited state before evaluating both alternatives, then lets application code select a result.
pages.success: The output identifies the selected branch and reports that two alternatives were evaluated. brawsr does not choose a winner or merge branch state.
